pois.name: Jalan Braga
pois.description: Bandung's most elegant colonial boulevard — the 'Champs-Élysées of the Dutch East Indies'. Art Deco buildings with decorated facades house a mix of galleries, bookshops, cafés, and boutique hotels. The city's heritage soul.

pois.name: Gedung Merdeka
pois.description: Site of the 1955 Asian-African Conference — the historic gathering where 29 newly-independent nations declared solidarity against colonialism. The Art Deco building (1895) is now a museum of the Bandung Conference with original furnishings preserved.

pois.name: Gedung Sate
pois.description: Bandung's most iconic building and the symbol of West Java province. The 1920 Dutch colonial headquarters features an ornamental central spire resembling satay skewers — the origin of its nickname. Home to the West Java Governor's office.

pois.name: Braga Permai Restaurant
pois.description: Bandung's most historic café, in a 1920s Art Deco building — once the Dutch colonial-era Maison Bogerijen. The wood-panelled interior and period photographs evoke old Bandoeng. Famous for its es krim (traditional ice cream).

pois.name: Museum Bank Indonesia Bandung
pois.description: The Bandung branch of Bank Indonesia's monetary history museum, housed in a 1920s Dutch bank building on Braga. Fine Art Deco interior with the original bank vault and colonial-era furniture.
